messages.content: New trip: Spokane distributor training. They want me there Thursday Feb. 19 for a product session and Friday morning for a partner check at the Spokane Valley warehouse. Can you build me a flight and hotel shortlist?
Sure. What time do you need to be on site Thursday, and do you want to fly home Friday after the partner check? Also, should I check all Bay Area airports or start with SFO?

Training starts at 1 p.m. Thursday, but I need to be in the warehouse by 9:30 for setup. Fly in Wednesday. Friday check should end around noon. Start with SFO, but include Oakland or San Jose if they’re materially better. No two-stop routing.
Got it. For the hotel, do you want to stay in Spokane Valley near the warehouse, or downtown Spokane with more restaurant choice? And is the demo case coming with you or getting shipped?

Warehouse is near Sullivan and I-90. Prefer Valley if the hotel is decent. I want parking, easy dinner, and guest ratings at 4.0 or better if possible. Fridge and coffee in the room would help. Demo case is the open question; it can ship to the distributor or maybe to the hotel.

Flight shortlist for Wednesday Feb. 18 into GEG: Best fit is United nonstop SFO-GEG, 1:10 p.m.-3:22 p.m. It gives you daylight arrival, no connection, and time to pick up a rental car or check the setup gear. Acceptable backup is Alaska SFO-SEA-GEG, 12:35 p.m.-4:28 p.m., with a 70-minute Seattle connection. Cleaner than most connections, but still a weather/connection exposure. Later option is Delta via Seattle, 3:05 p.m.-7:38 p.m.; I would not lead with it because it leaves little room if anything slips.
Is there anything after lunch that still lands before dinner, or is that United nonstop the one?

There is a United nonstop that is the practical after-lunch option: 1:10 p.m. departure, 3:22 p.m. arrival. The other later choices land closer to 7:30 or 8 and all connect through Seattle or Denver. For protecting Thursday setup, I’d keep the 1:10 nonstop as the main pick.
Okay, keep that as best fit. What about Friday home?

Friday Feb. 20 return options: Best fit is United nonstop GEG-SFO, 2:25 p.m.-4:42 p.m. If the warehouse check ends at noon, that is makeable with a normal drive to GEG, but it does not leave much room for a long lunch or equipment handoff. Acceptable backup is Alaska via Seattle, 4:05 p.m.-7:34 p.m., which gives a bigger cushion but adds a connection. I’d avoid the 12:40 p.m. departure; too tight from Spokane Valley.
Good. Show me hotels near the warehouse first. Downtown only if Valley looks weak.

Valley shortlist: 1. Oxford Suites Spokane Valley, about 4.5 Google rating, free parking, near I-90, on-site Bistro and lounge, plus nearby restaurants. Rooms generally include fridge, microwave, and coffee maker. Best fit for convenience and dinner. 2. Hampton Inn & Suites Spokane Valley, about 4.4 rating, free parking, breakfast, fridge and coffee in room, quick drive to Sullivan/I-90. More predictable business-hotel setup, less useful for dinner on property. 3. Mirabeau Park Hotel, about 4.2 rating, free parking, on-site restaurant, easy Valley access. Older property but practical if the first two price out.
Compare Oxford and Hampton plainly. I don’t care about downtown unless there’s a big quality gap.

Oxford is the better fit if you want one place to land, park, eat, and prep without driving again. It has stronger dinner convenience and a little more space. Hampton is the safer chain-standard backup: clean, good breakfast, easy parking, and usually straightforward early checkout, but you’ll probably drive for dinner. No big reason to go downtown unless rates in the Valley jump.
If the demo case ships to the hotel, which one is better? It’s a 45-pound Pelican case plus the literature box.

For that weight, I’d ask before sending it to a hotel. Oxford can receive guest packages, but a 45-pound equipment case may trigger a handling note or storage limitation. Hampton is similar: fine for small parcels, less ideal for gear. Best fit is shipping the demo case to the distributor if they can receive it Tuesday or Wednesday and lock it in the warehouse. Hotel is an acceptable backup for the literature box, not my first choice for the Pelican case.
Makes sense. Don’t book yet. If the distributor confirms receiving, what’s the clean plan?

Clean plan would be: fly United nonstop SFO-GEG Wednesday 1:10 p.m.-3:22 p.m.; rent a car at GEG; stay at Oxford Suites Spokane Valley Wednesday and Thursday nights; ship the Pelican case and literature box to the distributor for Tuesday/Wednesday delivery; return United nonstop GEG-SFO Friday 2:25 p.m.-4:42 p.m. That keeps the routing simple and the hotel close to the warehouse.
Can I realistically make the 2:25 return if Friday wraps at noon?

Yes, but it is a moderate cushion, not a huge one. Spokane Valley to GEG is usually about 25-30 minutes. If you leave the warehouse by 12:15, return the rental car quickly, and have no checked bag beyond normal work gear, the 2:25 nonstop is reasonable. If the partner check may run past 12:30, use the 4:05 Alaska backup.
Mark it that way. I need to confirm the distributor can receive the case and whether Friday might run late.

Marked, no booking made. Best fit: United nonstop SFO-GEG Wed Feb. 18, 1:10 p.m.-3:22 p.m.; Oxford Suites Spokane Valley for Feb. 18-20; United nonstop GEG-SFO Fri Feb. 20, 2:25 p.m.-4:42 p.m. Acceptable backup: Alaska return via Seattle at 4:05 p.m. if Friday may run late. Ask before booking: distributor package receiving for the 45-pound case, hotel rate/cancellation terms, and whether you’ll need checked baggage for any remaining equipment.
